candidate.answerReason: The cube has three groups of four parallel edges. Each group contributes six unordered pairs, giving 18 pairs.

methods.label: Group edges by direction
methods.explanation:
The cube's edges fall into three groups according to their directions:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\overline{AB},\ \overline{CD},\ \overline{EF},\ \overline{GH},\\
&\overline{AE},\ \overline{BF},\ \overline{CG},\ \overline{DH},\\
&\overline{AD},\ \overline{BC},\ \overline{EH},\ \overline{FG}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Any two edges in the same group are parallel, and edges from different groups are not parallel.

Within one group, pair the first edge with the other three, then pair the second edge with the two remaining edges, and finally pair the third with the fourth. This counts every pair once, giving \(3+2+1=6\) pairs per group.

Every parallel pair belongs to exactly one of the three groups, so the total is
\[
3\cdot6=18.
\]
The answer is \(18\), choice \(\text{C}\).
